name: English - Creative Writing C1: Introduction to Narrative Strategies and Literary Forms
description:
Sparking your Creativity: Exploring Varied Narrative Forms as a Tool to Improve Academic Writing and Rhetorical Skills

The ‘Introduction to Narrative Forms and Strategies’ course provides students with a stimulating overview of a range of narrative forms, tools and rhetorical devices. Some of the forms covered include contemporary nature writing, games narrative design and hybrid narrative essays. In the course, students will have the opportunity to experiment with some of these forms and try out many of the storytelling instruments and concepts first-hand.

Critical reading assignments focusing on the interplay between language, form and content will aid students in exploring the rules and strategies of composition used in both fiction and non-fiction genres and enable them to engage more closely with the English language to develop linguistic dexterity therein. 

Current theories of literary and cultural criticism will be introduced and students will be expected to critically evaluate model texts as well as their own writing whilst being encouraged to appraise, support and critique the writing of their peers in a guided workshop environment. 

A component covering revision and structural editing techniques will help prepare students for both academic and non-fiction publishing. 

The performative aspects of the writing industry including public performances and speaking (readings and discussions) will be touched upon and other issues related to being a writer i.e. the road to publication and the ethics of writing will also be discussed.
